label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration, drop-off

Last month I told Dana I would write this up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now done eight days of a civil trial, so here it is.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3.

Dropped off: Monday 10/19. Picked up: Tuesday 10/27. That is six business days against a quoted ten.

Work requested: full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning, firmware update.

Work done, per the invoice: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced, internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, internal battery replaced. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

Quoted: $285. Paid: $310. The extra $25 was the battery. Gloria Ruark, the technician, found it holding about 60% of rated capacity and emailed to say she would not replace it without my approval. I said yes. I would rather be asked than surprised on the invoice, and I was asked.

Paid personally, as I do with all my equipment. No reimbursement from the court.

Loaner: Yes, an Aria 2, handed over at drop-off without my having to ask.

The shop: Two people, off York Road in Towson. Parking in back is free, which counts for something if you have ever hauled a machine case very far.

How it held up: My first full day back in trial was expert testimony from an engineer who talks almost entirely in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke all day, and it has stayed clean for the rest of the trial. The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made. In all my years nobody has ever given me that, and I have kept it in the case.

What didn't go as well:

The loaner's tilt arm would not hold its position. It slipped in the middle of an afternoon deposition, and I spent the rest of the day with the machine propped on a legal pad. That is a nuisance, not a disaster, and I mentioned it when I wrote back about the battery. Gloria said they would repair it before it goes out again. If you take a loaner, though, check the tilt arm before you leave the shop.

The phones are the real weakness. The line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that is all. I called on Wednesday 10/21 to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box to leave a message in. Gloria emailed me the next day, so I was never actually left in the dark. But if you work a Monday docket, or you find a problem with a loaner on a Friday afternoon, you will not reach anyone by phone until Tuesday. Email is clearly how they work. Plan around that.

Dana, to your question: yes, I would trust them with your Aria. You have the same machine and the same number bar complaint I had. Mine was fixed properly, fixed early, and it has held up under the kind of testimony that would have shown it up if it hadn't been. I would put everything in writing at drop-off. Ask for the service sheet if they don't offer it, test the loaner before you leave the counter, and don't count on reaching them by phone at the end of the week.

Would I use them again? Yes. The bench work is careful and the billing is honest. The phone hours are what they are, and you should go in knowing that.

Maureen
